messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The standard error (i.e., the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under the null hypothesis) is  

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx 0.22 .
\]
message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but they provide sample mean, standard deviation, sample size, and population mean. They likely want the standard error? Actually they say "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". That might refer to the standard error of the sampling distribution under H0: sqrt(sigma^2/n). But we don't know sigma; we have sample std dev. So maybe use sample std dev as estimate of sigma. Then standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40)=6.3249. 1.4/6.3249=0.2215 approx.

But they also mention "for a population mean of 98.6." That might be irrelevant. They might want to calculate the standard deviation of the null distribution: sqrt((sigma^2)/n). Use sample std dev as sigma. So answer ~0.2215.

Alternatively, they might want to compute the standard deviation of the difference between sample mean and population mean? That would be sqrt((s^2 + sigma^2)/n)? No.

Given typical context, they'd ask for standard error. So answer: 0.2215.

We can also compute p-value using the function. But they didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation. So just give numeric.

Thus answer: 0.2215 (approx).
